Merge f5db2cfe02f1da9df8e61015eeef02987a730ac4 into d49ee0ce95ddef495c7948fd1526622b162b7b9b

fix(test): a test daemon's slot has one release, its exit, and its cleanups wait for that exit (f6eo)

TestDaemonProcess loses release() and spawnDaemonWithEnv loses its pool
parameter; exit-only release is tested on a /bin/sh stand-in. Cleanups await
the daemon's exit before removing its directories, signalDaemon treats the
EPERM macOS answers for an exited, unreaped group like ESRCH, a child error
after spawn is thrown, and the workflow check watches daemonCommand.

fix(test): a test daemon's pool slot is released by its exit alone, and its signal hears every refusal but ESRCH (f6eo)

The source entries share one constructor over production's daemonArgs and
daemonCommand. A signal no longer frees the machine-wide slot of a daemon it
leaves alive, a spawn resolves only once the process has a pid, the frozen
case reads the daemon's pid from its lease, and the readiness refusal tests
use an unsafe socket parent under the default entry.

fix(test): a test daemon runs on the arguments the client ships, and its signal is named for what it reaches (f6eo)

The source entry resolves tsx's loader through the package's exports and puts
it in front of the client's own daemon arguments, heap cap included. Because
the client refuses to spawn on a malformed memory budget, the tests of the
daemon's own refusal run it by hand. killTree becomes signalDaemon.

fix(test): a test daemon is node itself, so the signal that stops it reaches its shutdown (f6eo)

The tsx CLI relays a signal to a worker of its own and SIGKILLs that worker
if it has not answered within ~60 ms, so on a loaded runner a daemon stopped
with SIGTERM died before its handler restored tmux or released the registry.
Every process-tier daemon now runs as node with tsx's loader imported, through
the one spawn helper, so the pid a test holds and signals is the daemon's own.
The tmux-restore test adds the case that freezes the daemon across the
SIGTERM.

fix(doctor): a doctor click records whether it started a run or joined the one on its way (boii)

A doctor click while the session's run waits for its reading starts no
run, and nothing said so. Each doctor click now notes on its record
doctorRun=started|joined and doctorRunName, the run it asked.

The effect-refresh e2e drops the click that judged the same at-rest bar
under the same menu as the one before it, so it expects three runs. After
each click it waits for that run's note in the log, which is the source its
final assertion reads, and every row that moves is matched by one constant
for the full reason.

fix(test): each doctor click in the e2e waits for the run before it to report (boii)

A doctor click while the session's run still waits for its reading starts
no run, so two clicks one draw apart logged one or two runs depending on how
fast the host read the machine. The effect-refresh case now draws its row
back after each click before clicking again, and the URL-handler case waits
for its run's row instead of reading the first draw. Under a 1.5 s delay on
the host's reading, the old effect-refresh case logs three runs and fails;
both cases pass.

fix(launch): a repository reader's children read each session's repository, not the shell's that started it (9gbg)

git finds its repository from GIT_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE and the other names
`git rev-parse --local-env-vars` prints, ahead of its working directory,
and gh honours GH_REPO. A daemon, doctor, check or plugin install started
from a git hook, a `rebase --exec` or a vcsh shell read every session's
branch, status and PR from that shell's repository.

A launch scope now names what its children do not inherit. The child
environment is the inherited environment, read at each launch, less those
names, under each launch's overlay: one place for every launch form. The
process's own environment is untouched, since it is also what the process
reports as the session's.

The daemon, doctor, check and plugin install ask git once, as they start,
and withhold its names and GH_REPO; the relay and every other process ask
nothing. A git that cannot answer (or an old one that echoes the flag) is a
fault carrying git's words: the daemon logs it, still starts and draws, and
stands a warning on every bar through its launcher's facts; the doctor
fails a new "repository reads" row; plugin install exits 1 with the reason.
Plugin install's own overlay that unset the same names is gone. The Pages
site's simulated git answers the ask.
